name: US Fed Funds (effective)
definition: The volume-weighted rate US banks actually pay for overnight funds — where the Fed's policy setting meets the market. It sits inside the announced target range.
why_on_board: The anchor for every dollar rate, including the short-term rates that set the fund's ILS→USD hedge economics.
what_a_rise_means: Policy tightening: dollar cash pays more, bond prices under pressure, hedging shekels back to dollars pays more.
what_a_fall_means: Policy easing: duration rallies and the hedge pickup shrinks.
read_with: Fed funds, market-implied path, US−Israel rate differential

name: US market-implied rate path
definition: The one-year Treasury bill yield minus the effective fed funds rate, in percentage points. A rough market forecast of where policy goes over the next year — negative means cuts are priced.
why_on_board: It converts 'what will the Fed do' from opinion into a number. When the priced path and the Fed's rhetoric disagree, bond volatility follows.
what_a_rise_means: The market prices tightening (or fewer cuts): front-end yields rising.
what_a_fall_means: The market prices easing: cuts expected within a year.
read_with: Fed funds, US 1Y, MOVE

name: US real policy rate
definition: The effective fed funds rate minus CPI inflation over the past year, in percentage points. It answers whether policy is actually restrictive after inflation.
source: Derived: fed funds minus US CPI YoY (latest print)
why_on_board: A 4% policy rate means opposite things at 2% and at 6% inflation. The real rate is the cleaner measure of how hard policy is braking the economy that Israeli assets ultimately trade against.
what_a_rise_means: Policy is getting more restrictive in real terms — a brake on growth and on risk assets.
what_a_fall_means: Real policy is loosening, whether by cuts or by inflation catching up.
read_with: US CPI, Fed funds, 10Y real yield

name: US 3M (bill)
definition: The three-month Treasury bill yield — the risk-free dollar rate over a quarter, and the standard tenor for FX-hedging arithmetic.
why_on_board: This is the dollar leg of the fund's hedge: the implied cost of hedging shekels back to dollars is the 3M rate differential. It is also the cash yield the fund's dollar liquidity earns.
what_a_rise_means: Short dollar rates up: cash pays more and the hedge pickup on shekel exposure widens.
what_a_fall_means: Short rates down: cash drag falls, hedge pickup narrows.
read_with: Israel Makam 3M, implied hedge cost, rate differential

name: US 1Y (bill)
definition: The one-year Treasury bill yield. Because it spans the next year of Fed meetings, it embeds the market's expected policy path.
why_on_board: The cleanest single input for the implied-path row: it says what the market believes the Fed averages over the next twelve months.
what_a_rise_means: The market lifts its one-year rate view — fewer cuts or more hikes priced.
what_a_fall_means: The market lowers the path — more easing priced.
read_with: Market-implied rate path, Fed funds

name: US 2Y
definition: The two-year Treasury yield — the tenor most sensitive to the policy cycle over the next couple of years.
why_on_board: The short leg of the term spread and the market's summary of the whole cutting (or hiking) cycle, not just the next meeting.
what_a_rise_means: The cycle repriced hawkish.
what_a_fall_means: The cycle repriced dovish.
read_with: US 10Y, term spread, market-implied path

name: US 10Y
definition: The ten-year Treasury yield — the world's benchmark risk-free rate and the base rate under most long-dated dollar assets, including Israel's USD sovereign bonds.
why_on_board: Israel's USD spread row is measured against this yield, and the fund's Israel 10Y vs US 10Y comparison is the core relative-value frame of the strategy.
what_a_rise_means: The global discount rate rose: bond prices down everywhere, spread product repriced.
what_a_fall_means: The discount rate fell: duration rallied.
read_with: Israel 10Y, Israel USD spread, term spread, 10Y real yield · breakeven

name: US term spread (10Y − 2Y)
definition: The ten-year yield minus the two-year yield, in basis points. Negative — an inverted curve — has historically preceded US recessions.
why_on_board: The shape of the US curve sets the template global bond investors apply to Israel's curve, and steepening/flattening moves drive the relative performance of the fund's duration positioning.
what_a_rise_means: Steepening: markets price more growth or more term premium; long bonds underperform.
what_a_fall_means: Flattening or inversion: late-cycle pricing; recession odds rising.
read_with: US 2Y, US 10Y, Israel term spread

name: US 10Y real yield · breakeven
definition: The ten-year yield split into its two parts: the TIPS real yield (compensation after inflation) and the breakeven (the inflation the market expects). Real plus breakeven equals the nominal 10Y.
why_on_board: The split says WHY yields moved. A sell-off driven by real yields hits all assets; one driven by breakevens mainly repriced inflation — very different signals for an Israel/US bond book.
what_a_rise_means: Rising means the market prices more US inflation.
what_a_fall_means: Falling breakeven: disinflation priced in.
read_with: US 10Y, US CPI, Israel 10Y breakeven

name: US CPI (YoY)
definition: The US consumer price index, measured as the change over the past twelve months. It is the headline inflation figure the Federal Reserve is judged against, published monthly by the BLS.
why_on_board: US inflation sets the Fed's path, and the Fed's path sets the dollar rates every Israeli bond is ultimately priced against. For a fund hedging shekel exposure back to dollars, the US price level is half of the hedge-cost equation.
what_a_rise_means: Inflation is running hotter: the Fed stays tighter for longer, Treasury yields and hedge costs tend to rise, and bond prices fall.
what_a_fall_means: Inflation is cooling: rate cuts come closer, yields tend to fall and bond prices rise.
read_with: US PCE, Fed funds, US 10Y, 10Y breakeven

name: US PCE (YoY)
definition: The personal-consumption-expenditures price index over twelve months — the Fed's stated inflation target measure (2%). It runs cooler than CPI because its basket adjusts as consumers substitute.
source: FRED (PCEPI, percent change from year ago)
why_on_board: When CPI and PCE disagree, the Fed follows PCE. Watching both avoids over-reading a CPI print the Fed will look through.
what_a_rise_means: The Fed's own gauge is above target: policy stays restrictive, supporting the dollar and raising the bar for cuts.
what_a_fall_means: The target measure is easing: cuts become defensible even if headline CPI is noisy.
read_with: US CPI, Fed funds, market-implied rate path

name: Bank of Israel rate
definition: The Bank of Israel's policy interest rate, set at scheduled rate decisions roughly every six to seven weeks.
why_on_board: The anchor of every shekel rate the fund's managers trade, and the Israeli leg of the hedge-cost equation.
what_a_rise_means: BoI tightening: shekel cash and short Makam yields rise; bond prices pressured; hedge cost for a US investor falls.
what_a_fall_means: BoI easing: local duration rallies; the hedge pickup for dollar-based investors widens.
read_with: Israel CPI, implied rate path, US−Israel differential

name: Israel market-implied rate path
definition: The one-year Makam (T-bill) yield minus the Bank of Israel rate, in percentage points. Negative means the market prices cuts over the next year.
why_on_board: It shows what the local market believes about BoI before the decisions happen — the expectations the fund's managers are positioned around.
what_a_rise_means: The market prices a higher BoI path.
what_a_fall_means: More cuts priced into the shekel curve.
read_with: BoI rate, Makam 1Y, US implied path

name: Israel real policy rate
definition: The Bank of Israel rate minus Israeli CPI inflation over the past year, in percentage points.
source: Derived: BoI rate minus Israel CPI YoY (latest print)
why_on_board: Whether Israeli policy is genuinely restrictive determines how much room local bonds have to rally — a key input to the fund's duration view.
what_a_rise_means: Real tightening: policy biting harder in Israel.
what_a_fall_means: Real loosening: easier conditions for Israeli credit and duration.
read_with: BoI rate, Israel CPI, US real policy rate

name: Israel Makam (1Y)
definition: The one-year Makam — the Bank of Israel's own short-term bill — yield. The shekel market's one-year risk-free rate.
source: Bank of Israel API (daily T-bill yield)
why_on_board: The local cash benchmark and the Israeli leg of the implied-path row; short-duration Israeli funds are priced off it.
what_a_rise_means: Front-end shekel rates rising — tighter path priced.
what_a_fall_means: Front-end rallying — cuts priced.
read_with: BoI rate, implied rate path, US 1Y

name: Israel 2Y
definition: The two-year benchmark Israeli government bond yield to maturity (IL2YT=RR, Tel Aviv quote), daily close.
why_on_board: The short leg of Israel's term spread and the cycle-sensitive tenor of the shekel curve the managers trade.
what_a_rise_means: The local rate cycle repriced hawkish.
what_a_fall_means: The local cycle repriced dovish.
read_with: Israel 10Y, Israel term spread

name: Israel 10Y
definition: The ten-year benchmark Israeli government bond yield to maturity (IL10YT=RR, Tel Aviv quote), daily close — history since 2002. The benchmark long rate of the shekel market; it sits a few basis points from the BoI's fitted zero-coupon rate, which stays on the Excel as a monthly reference column.
why_on_board: The single most important price for the strategy: it anchors Israeli government and corporate bond valuations, and its spread to the US 10Y summarises Israel's local risk premium.
what_a_rise_means: Israeli long yields up: local duration losing, risk premium or inflation expectations rising.
what_a_fall_means: Long yields down: local bond market rallying.
read_with: US 10Y, US−Israel differential, 10Y real yield · breakeven, Tel Gov Shekel

name: Israel term spread (10Y − 2Y)
definition: Israel's ten-year yield minus its two-year yield, in basis points, from the daily benchmark bond yields.
why_on_board: The slope of the shekel curve is where the managers' curve positioning lives — and comparing it with the US slope shows whether Israel is marching to its own cycle.
what_a_rise_means: Local curve steepening: term premium or growth expectations rising.
what_a_fall_means: Local curve flattening: late-cycle or heavy demand for long duration.
read_with: US term spread, Israel 2Y, Israel 10Y

name: Israel 10Y real yield · breakeven
definition: Israel's ten-year split into the CPI-linked real yield and the implied breakeven (nominal minus real) — the inflation rate at which linkers and nominals return the same.
source: Derived: BoI nominal and CPI-linked zero-coupon curves
why_on_board: Israel's bond market is unusually rich in CPI-linked paper, so the linker/nominal split is a live allocation decision for every manager in the book — this row is that decision's price.
what_a_rise_means: The market prices more Israeli inflation; CPI-linked bonds outperform nominal ones.
what_a_fall_means: The market prices less inflation; nominal bonds outperform linkers.
read_with: Israel CPI, Israel 10Y, Tel Bond-60 vs Tel Bond Shekel

name: Israel USD 2-year
definition: The yield to maturity at the two-year point of Israel's US-dollar sovereign bonds (State of Israel globals), interpolated between the quoted issues nearest that tenor.
why_on_board: Israel's dollar curve strips the shekel out of Israel risk: it shows what the market charges for Israeli credit alone at the short end.
what_a_rise_means: Short-tenor Israel USD yields rising — funding or credit premium up.
what_a_fall_means: Short-tenor dollar funding for Israel getting cheaper.
read_with: US 2Y, Israel USD 10-year, 5Y CDS

name: Israel USD 10-year
definition: The yield to maturity at the ten-year point of Israel's US-dollar sovereign curve, interpolated between the quoted globals bracketing that tenor.
why_on_board: The long point of Israel's dollar curve — the basis of the USD spread row, and directly comparable to the US 10Y with no currency adjustment.
what_a_rise_means: Israel's long-dollar borrowing cost rising.
what_a_fall_means: The market lending Israel long dollars more cheaply.
read_with: US 10Y, Israel USD spread, 10Y CDS

name: Israel CPI (YoY)
definition: Israel's consumer price index over the past twelve months, published by the CBS. The Bank of Israel targets 1–3%.
source: Bank of Israel API (CBS general index, YoY computed here)
why_on_board: Israeli inflation drives the Bank of Israel's rate, the shekel curve, and the CPI-linked half of the local bond market — the direct backdrop for every manager the fund allocates to.
what_a_rise_means: Inflation is picking up: BoI cuts get pushed out, nominal yields rise, and CPI-linked bonds outperform nominals.
what_a_fall_means: Disinflation: room for BoI cuts, shekel duration rallies, linkers lag nominals.
read_with: Bank of Israel rate, Israel 10Y breakeven, Tel Bond-60 (CPI linked)

name: CPI drivers (contributions, pp)
definition: Headline Israel CPI YoY decomposed into what drove it: housing, food (ex-fruit & veg), fruit & vegetables, energy (household electricity + vehicle fuel) and a residual for everything else, each as weight × component YoY in percentage points, summing to headline exactly. Weights: housing and fruit & veg are implied per basket year from the CBS's own excluding-indices (the published weights file is not machine-readable — the CBS pages render as JS shells; the implied medians land within ~0.3pp of the published 2025-basket weights, housing 27.3% vs ~27.1%, F&V 3.5% vs ~3.4%); food, electricity and vehicle-fuel weights are the published CBS constants per basket year. The residual closes the identity, so any weight error lands there rather than in the headline. The food/electricity/fuel constants are refreshed annually per the README's Manual refresh checklist (next: the 2027 basket, with the January-2027 CPI, ~mid-Feb 2027); if a new basket year's CPI lands first, the row flags itself 'Weights stale' and keeps computing on the latest entered basket.
source: CBS price-index API (component indices; decomposition computed here)
why_on_board: Shows WHAT is driving Israeli inflation, not just how much of it there is — whether a print is housing, food, the volatile fruit-and-veg leg or imported energy changes what the BoI does about it. Research/blog block, not part of the investor letter.
what_a_rise_means: Read per band: a housing-led rise is sticky and rate-sensitive; an energy-led rise imports Brent and the shekel and tends to pass; a broad residual rise is underlying inflation the BoI must answer.
what_a_fall_means: Falling contributions concentrated in energy or fruit & veg are noise the BoI looks through; a falling residual and housing band is genuine disinflation and room to cut.
read_with: Israel CPI (YoY), CPI ex-energy, Bank of Israel rate, Brent in ILS

name: CPI ex-energy (YoY)
definition: The CBS special index excluding energy (code 110045, published since 2007), YoY — Israel's closest official cut to a core-ex-energy read.
why_on_board: One line answers the first question about any CPI print: was it energy? The gap to headline is the energy effect in index form.
what_a_rise_means: Underlying (non-energy) inflation is firming regardless of what oil did.
what_a_fall_means: Core pressure easing even if pump and tariff prices are noisy.
read_with: Israel CPI (YoY), CPI drivers, CPI vehicle fuel, CPI household electricity

name: CPI housing (YoY)
definition: The CBS housing group (120450) YoY — mostly rent and owner-occupied housing services, the largest single weight in the basket (~26-27%, implied per basket year). Rent (120460) and owner-occupied (120490) ride the export tab.
why_on_board: The heaviest and stickiest CPI component: where housing YoY goes, headline eventually follows, and the BoI knows it.
what_a_rise_means: Rent renewals repricing up — sticky inflation that outlasts energy swings and keeps the BoI hawkish.
what_a_fall_means: The rental market cooling — the slowest-moving disinflation force finally working.
read_with: CPI drivers, Israel CPI (YoY), Bank of Israel rate

name: CPI food ex-fruit & veg (YoY)
definition: The CBS food group excluding fruit and vegetables (120050), YoY — the processed and packaged food basket, weight ~15% (published CBS constant per basket year).
why_on_board: The most politically visible component — food price rounds (and the import-reform pressure against them) move this line, and its weight makes it matter.
what_a_rise_means: Supplier price rounds sticking — broad, visible inflation households feel immediately.
what_a_fall_means: Competition and import reform biting, or commodity cost relief passing through.
read_with: CPI drivers, CPI fruit & vegetables, Israel CPI (YoY)

name: CPI fruit & vegetables (YoY)
definition: The CBS fruit and vegetables group (120040), YoY — the basket's most volatile leg (weight ~3.4%, implied per basket year), swung by harvests, weather and import quotas; the CBS itself strips it in its ex-F&V special index.
why_on_board: Small weight, outsized print-day noise: knowing a surprise was fruit & veg stops a false read of the trend.
what_a_rise_means: Usually weather or supply noise, not trend — look through it unless it persists.
what_a_fall_means: Harvest/import relief; a mechanical drag on the next prints.
read_with: CPI drivers, CPI food ex-fruit & veg, Israel CPI (YoY)

name: CPI household electricity (YoY)
definition: The CBS household electricity item (120590), YoY — the regulated Electricity Authority tariff in official index form (the Authority's own tariff files are not machine-readable: probe rounds 35-36 tried the API, file URLs and HTML before settling on the CPI item).
why_on_board: The regulated half of the energy contribution: tariff updates land in discrete, pre-announced steps, so this line separates policy-set energy inflation from market-set fuel.
what_a_rise_means: A tariff update passing generation costs (gas, coal, FX) into households — stepwise, not gradual.
what_a_fall_means: Tariff cuts handing energy relief straight to the CPI.
read_with: CPI drivers, European natural gas TTF, CPI vehicle fuel

name: CPI vehicle fuel (YoY)
definition: The CBS vehicle fuel, charging and oils item (140690), YoY — the pump price in CPI form, driven by Brent in shekels and the (mostly fixed, per-liter) excise.
why_on_board: The market half of the energy contribution and the fastest Brent-to-CPI channel — pump prices reset monthly off the regulated formula.
what_a_rise_means: Brent in ILS feeding through — imported inflation the BoI mostly looks through unless it broadens.
what_a_fall_means: Oil or shekel relief hitting the next prints mechanically.
read_with: Brent in ILS, 95 octane ex-refinery, CPI drivers

name: Brent crude ($)
definition: Brent front-month future, dollars per barrel, daily close (Yahoo BZ=F). Primary by the round-38 sanity check: FRED's DCOILBRENTEU ran $20-26 above the traded future in Oct 2026 (and $9-33 over the prior 60 days) — FRED is kept only as a hidden cross-check column whose gap is LOGGED on every run (no row flag). The board's WTI row is the same source family (Yahoo CL=F), so the Brent-WTI spread shown is futures against futures; that spread is genuinely wide and volatile — $3-13 with a mean near $7 over the 60 days to Oct 2026 — not a fixed few dollars.
source: Yahoo (BZ=F); FRED DCOILBRENTEU as logged cross-check
why_on_board: Israel prices fuel off Brent, not WTI — this is the oil leg of the inflation-drivers block in the currency it trades in.
what_a_rise_means: Imported energy inflation building; pump and tariff pressure one to two months out.
what_a_fall_means: Energy disinflation in the pipeline for the fuel and electricity items.
read_with: Brent in ILS, WTI crude, CPI vehicle fuel

name: Brent in ILS (₪)
definition: Brent (BZ=F) multiplied by the BoI USD/ILS representative rate, daily — the shekel oil price the local fuel items actually follow, derived here from the two parent rows.
why_on_board: The CPI doesn't care whether pump pressure came from oil or the shekel — this line is the single series that combines both, the true upstream of the vehicle-fuel item.
what_a_rise_means: Oil up, shekel down, or both — fuel-led CPI pressure either way.
what_a_fall_means: A stronger shekel can hand Israel energy disinflation even with oil flat.
read_with: Brent crude ($), USD/ILS, CPI vehicle fuel, 95 octane ex-refinery

name: European natural gas TTF (€/MWh)
definition: The Dutch TTF front-month natural gas future, euros per MWh, daily close (Yahoo TTF=F). FRED's monthly EU gas price (PNGASEUUSDM, $/MMBtu) rides hidden as a logged cross-check, converted to €/MWh before comparing. Israel's own generation mix and domestic gas production were dropped from scope — Noga publishes only dashboard animations, no fetchable history (probe round 36).
source: Yahoo (TTF=F); FRED PNGASEUUSDM as converted cross-check
why_on_board: The global gas benchmark behind generation costs and the electricity-tariff updates — the upstream of the regulated half of energy CPI.
what_a_rise_means: Generation cost pressure that reaches households through the next tariff update.
what_a_fall_means: Tariff-cut room building at the Electricity Authority.
read_with: CPI household electricity, Brent crude ($)

name: 95 octane, ex-refinery (ILS/kl)
definition: The regulated 95-octane gasoline price, pipeline-delivered, in ILS per kiloliter EX-REFINERY — before excise, marketing margin and VAT — from the Ministry of Energy datasets on data.gov.il, monthly from 2020-01. NOT the pump price: the pump-price announcement page sits behind a bot wall (probe round 35), so the CPI vehicle-fuel item carries the pump read and this row carries the upstream formula input.
source: data.gov.il CKAN (Ministry of Energy, orl datasets)
why_on_board: The official formula input between Brent-in-ILS and the pump: it isolates how much pump movement is raw cost versus excise and margins.
what_a_rise_means: The regulated formula passing Brent-in-ILS through — pump and CPI fuel follow within the month.
what_a_fall_means: Cost relief in the pipeline before taxes mute it at the pump.
read_with: Brent in ILS, CPI vehicle fuel, CPI drivers

name: US − Israel rate differential
definition: The gap between US and Israeli rates at three points: policy rate, 3-month bills and 10-year bonds, in basis points. Positive means the US pays more.
source: Derived from the policy, 3M and 10Y rows
why_on_board: The differential is the price of being in shekels for a dollar-based fund: it sets hedge economics, drives the shekel, and frames Israel-vs-US relative value at every tenor.
what_a_rise_means: The US pays ever more over Israel: hedging shekels is better paid, but local yields look less competitive.
what_a_fall_means: The gap narrowing: Israeli yields more competitive; hedge pickup shrinking.
read_with: Implied hedge cost, USD/ILS, Israel 10Y, US 10Y

name: Implied ILS→USD hedge (ann.)
definition: The annualised percentage a US investor earns (positive) or pays (negative) to hedge shekel exposure back to dollars, implied from the 3-month rate differential under covered interest parity. Actual forward points are not sourced.
source: Derived: US 3M bill minus Israel 3M Makam
why_on_board: Kotel's returns are dollar returns: whether shekel assets are worth holding hedged depends directly on this number. When the hedge pays, Israeli yield can be bought with the currency risk removed — and paid for doing it.
what_a_rise_means: The hedge pays a US investor more — hedged Israeli bonds become more attractive in dollar terms.
what_a_fall_means: The pickup shrinks or turns negative: hedging starts to cost, and the case for Israeli bonds has to rest on spread rather than yield.
read_with: US−Israel differential, US 3M, USD/ILS

name: US IG OAS
definition: The option-adjusted spread of the ICE BofA US investment-grade corporate index over Treasuries, in basis points — the extra yield for holding quality US credit.
why_on_board: The base price of credit risk in the world's deepest market. Israeli spreads rarely stay tight when US IG widens; when it widens, Israeli spreads almost always follow; it is the global credit backdrop every position in the book sits against.
what_a_rise_means: Credit risk repricing wider: risk-off, spread product under pressure globally.
what_a_fall_means: Spreads grinding tighter: benign credit conditions, carry strategies rewarded.
read_with: US HY OAS, Israel USD spread, 5Y CDS

name: US HY OAS
definition: The option-adjusted spread of the ICE BofA US high-yield index over Treasuries, in basis points — the price of risky corporate credit.
why_on_board: High yield moves first and hardest when credit turns. It is the early-warning line for the credit cycle Israeli corporates also live in.
what_a_rise_means: Stress building in risky credit; watch for contagion into EM and Israeli spreads.
what_a_fall_means: Risk appetite healthy; carry environment supportive.
read_with: US IG OAS, MOVE · VIX, Israel corporate spread (Phase 3)

name: MOVE · VIX
definition: The two standard volatility gauges: MOVE for Treasury options (rates volatility) and VIX for S&P 500 options (equity volatility).
why_on_board: For a bond fund, MOVE is the more honest fear gauge — rate volatility drives spread volatility and hedge costs. VIX alongside shows whether stress is rates-led or equity-led.
what_a_rise_means: Numeric series is the VIX: rising volatility, de-risking, wider spreads likely.
what_a_fall_means: Volatility compressing: carry and spread positions breathe easier.
read_with: US IG/HY OAS, term spread

name: Israel USD spread to US Treasury
definition: Israel's interpolated ten-year US-dollar sovereign yield minus the US ten-year Treasury yield, in basis points — Israel's pure credit premium in dollars, with no currency component.
why_on_board: The cleanest market price of 'Israel risk' for a dollar investor — the number the fund's whole premise (earning Israeli premium in dollar terms) stands on.
what_a_rise_means: The market charges more for Israel risk: geopolitics, fiscal or ratings pressure.
what_a_fall_means: Israel risk repricing tighter: confidence returning; local assets usually follow.
read_with: 5Y and 10Y CDS, US 10Y, sovereign ratings footnote

name: Israel 5Y CDS
definition: The five-year credit-default-swap premium on Israel's dollar debt, in basis points a year — the market price of insuring against an Israeli sovereign default over five years.
source: entered by hand from the month-end quote
why_on_board: The benchmark tenor for sovereign risk and the fastest read the market gives on Israel: it reprices on geopolitics within hours. On this board it is a month-end figure.
what_a_rise_means: Insurance on Israel costs more: risk premium widening; expect spread and shekel pressure.
what_a_fall_means: Israel risk normalising: spreads and the shekel usually firm together.
read_with: Israel USD spread, 10Y CDS, sovereign ratings footnote

name: Israel 10Y CDS
definition: The ten-year credit-default-swap premium on Israel, in basis points a year — long-horizon default insurance.
source: Desk-entered monthly (no free feed); history seeded from Investing.com
why_on_board: The 10Y-vs-5Y CDS slope says whether the market fears an event soon or a slow erosion — context the 5Y alone can't give.
what_a_rise_means: Long-horizon Israel risk repricing wider.
what_a_fall_means: Structural confidence in Israel improving.
read_with: 5Y CDS, Israel USD spread

name: Israel corporate spread
definition: The Bank of Israel's monthly spread of the Tel Bond Shekel corporate bond index over the government curve, in basis points. Tel Bond constituents are rated at least A− by Maalot or A3 by Midroog, so this is the price of investment-grade corporate risk in the local market.
source: Bank of Israel (SECDWH, Tel Bond Shekel spread)
why_on_board: The corporate spread is the piece of the local risk premium the fund's managers actually harvest — Tel Bond yields over govies. It completes the chain: US credit → Israel sovereign → Israel corporate.
what_a_rise_means: Israeli companies are paying more over the government to borrow: credit conditions tightening, existing holdings marked down, better entry yields for new money.
what_a_fall_means: Corporate borrowing costs narrowing toward the government's: holdings gain, future returns from spread shrink.
read_with: Tel Bond-60, Tel Bond Shekel, US IG OAS

name: Foreign ownership: government bonds
definition: Nonresidents' share of the market value of tradable Israeli government bonds, from the Bank of Israel's monthly distribution-of-holders file (New Report, NIS billion by holder). Before January 2020 the series is the Old Report's percentage shares — the January 2020 splice is a change of basis, not a market move.
source: Bank of Israel distribution-of-holders files — manual monthly upload (benchmarks/sponsor_data/BOI_HOLDERS/)
why_on_board: Foreign demand is the marginal buyer of Israeli duration: when nonresidents add, the risk premium compresses, and their exit is the classic stress tell.
what_a_rise_means: Foreign investors adding Israeli government duration; spreads usually tighten.
what_a_fall_means: Foreign money leaving the shekel curve — read it with the CDS and the USD spread.
read_with: Israel 5Y CDS, Israel USD 10Y spread to UST, Israel 10Y

name: Pension + provident share
definition: Pension funds plus provident and advanced-study funds, as a share of government-bond market value (New Report, from 2020).
source: Bank of Israel distribution-of-holders files — manual monthly upload (benchmarks/sponsor_data/BOI_HOLDERS/)
why_on_board: The domestic institutional bid that absorbs issuance when foreigners step back — the mirror image of the nonresident row above it.
what_a_rise_means: Local institutions absorbing more of the stock.
what_a_fall_means: Locals ceding share — to the Bank of Israel, banks or foreigners.
read_with: Foreign ownership: government bonds

name: Bank of Israel share
definition: The Bank of Israel's own holdings as a share of government-bond market value (New Report, from 2020) — the footprint of the 2020-21 purchase programme running off.
source: Bank of Israel distribution-of-holders files — manual monthly upload (benchmarks/sponsor_data/BOI_HOLDERS/)
why_on_board: Central-bank holdings distort the foreign/domestic split; knowing the Bank's share keeps the rows above honest.
what_a_rise_means: The Bank absorbing bonds (easing or reinvestment).
what_a_fall_means: The QE stock running off — more float for the market to hold.
read_with: Foreign ownership: government bonds, Israel 10Y

name: Foreign ownership: corporate bonds
definition: Nonresidents' share of the market value of tradable Israeli corporate bonds (New Report; Old Report percentages from 2005 before the January 2020 splice).
source: Bank of Israel distribution-of-holders files — manual monthly upload (benchmarks/sponsor_data/BOI_HOLDERS/)
why_on_board: Foreign participation in Tel Bond credit is thin, so moves in this low single-digit share say more about global appetite for Israel risk than any index level.
what_a_rise_means: Foreign money reaching down into Israeli credit — a strong risk-appetite signal.
what_a_fall_means: Foreigners retreating to sovereigns only, or out entirely.
read_with: Israel corporate spread, Tel Bond-60 CPI Linked

name: Foreign ownership: makam
definition: Nonresidents' share of makam (central-bank bill) market value (New Report; Old Report percentages from 1995 before the January 2020 splice).
source: Bank of Israel distribution-of-holders files — manual monthly upload (benchmarks/sponsor_data/BOI_HOLDERS/)
why_on_board: Makam is the classic hot-money instrument: the nonresident share is the fastest gauge of speculative shekel inflows — the carry trade in one number.
what_a_rise_means: Hot money flowing into shekel bills — shekel-supportive but flighty.
what_a_fall_means: The carry trade unwinding; it tends to show up in USD/ILS within weeks.
read_with: USD / ILS, ILS basket (nominal effective), Bank of Israel rate

name: Israel sovereign ratings (footnote)
definition: Israel's long-term foreign-currency ratings: S&P A, stable outlook (outlook raised from negative, November 2025); Moody's Baa1, stable outlook (raised from negative, January 2026); Fitch A, negative outlook (affirmed March 2026). Update this entry by hand when an agency acts.
source: S&P, Moody's, Fitch public announcements — manual
why_on_board: Ratings gate which investors may hold Israel at all: a downgrade forces selling by mandate-constrained funds regardless of price, so the outlook column is an early warning for the spread rows above.
what_a_rise_means: An upgrade or outlook improvement: forced-seller risk recedes; spreads usually tighten.
what_a_fall_means: A downgrade: index exclusions and forced selling can widen spreads beyond fundamentals.
read_with: Israel USD spread, 5Y/10Y CDS

name: Institutional FX exposure
definition: Israeli institutional investors' (pension, provident, insurance) exposure to foreign exchange including NIS/FX derivatives, as a percent of total assets. Source stores fractions; the board shows percent. Some 2024 observations are withheld by the BoI pending a reporter correction and appear as gaps.
source: BoI mosadiyim_l1e.xlsx — automated download (stable boi_files URL)
why_on_board: When institutions hedge less FX or lift foreign exposure, shekels leave the local bond market; this is the demand backdrop for every Israeli bond position.
what_a_rise_means: Institutions running more FX risk — typically less local-bond demand at the margin.
what_a_fall_means: Hedging back into shekels — flow support for local assets.
read_with: Institutional foreign-asset exposure, Net institutional FX transactions, USD / ILS

name: Institutional foreign-asset exposure
definition: Institutional investors' exposure to foreign assets as a percent of total assets (balance-sheet foreign assets plus foreign futures and derivatives). Monthly since 2002.
why_on_board: The structural allocation shift abroad is the single biggest drag on domestic bond demand over the last decade — this row is that trend in one number.
what_a_rise_means: More of the pension shekel invested abroad; less structural local-bond demand.
what_a_fall_means: Repatriation — a tailwind for Israeli duration and the shekel.
read_with: Institutional FX exposure, Institutional holdings: government bonds

name: Institutional portfolio: Israeli equity share
definition: Tradable Israeli shares as a share of institutional investors' TOTAL assets, % — asset-weighted across the seven institutional investor types in the BoI asset-portfolio file shce28 (provident & severance, advanced-study, old pension, new general and new comprehensive pension, assured-yield and profit-sharing life insurance; mutual funds are in the file but excluded from the aggregate, matching the insurance + pension + provident universe of the holdings rows). Monthly since 2001; automated download. Aug 2026: 12.3%, up from 8.9% in Jan 2023. ETNs tracking share indices are NOT included — they track foreign indices too — and ride the export as their own column. NOTE THE CONCEPT: % of the institutions' own portfolio, not % of the equity market.
why_on_board: The direct test of whether repatriated money is going into Israeli equities rather than bonds: the share of the portfolio parked in local shares.
what_a_rise_means: Institutions allocating toward Israeli equities (flows and/or local outperformance).
what_a_fall_means: Rotation away from local shares — toward bonds, deposits or foreign assets.
read_with: Institutional portfolio: Israeli tradable bond share, Institutional foreign-asset exposure, TA-125

name: Institutional portfolio: Israeli tradable bond share
definition: Tradable government plus corporate bonds as a share of institutional assets, % (same aggregation as the equity-share row; the display shows the two legs). Aug 2026: 15.3% (gov 9.6% · corp 5.7%), down from 16.7% in Jan 2023 and ~32% in 2001. DISTINCT FROM 'Institutional share of bonds outstanding' (38.7%): that row divides institutional holdings by the BOND MARKET'S size; this one divides by the INSTITUTIONS' OWN assets. CONTEXT, THE DESIGNATED-BOND REFORM: from October 2022 the Treasury stopped issuing new non-tradable designated bonds to the pension funds, replacing them with a yield-assurance mechanism, so the designated stock rolls off as it matures — visible in the export's non-tradable government column falling from 21.5% of assets (Jan 2023) to 14.0% (Aug 2026); money rolling off designated bonds must be reinvested somewhere, which is why the tradable-bond and equity shares are read together.
why_on_board: The bond leg of the allocation story: whether the portfolio is rotating toward or away from the local bond market that the supply rows below must clear.
what_a_rise_means: Institutions allocating toward local tradable bonds.
what_a_fall_means: Rotation away from local bonds — toward equities, foreign assets or cash.
read_with: Institutional portfolio: Israeli equity share, Institutional share of bonds outstanding, Net new supply (est., ex-price)

name: Net institutional FX transactions
definition: Net foreign-currency transactions by institutional investors, $bn per quarter. SIGN CONVENTION: positive = net FX purchases (money moving offshore), negative = net FX sales (repatriation, shekel-supportive). Typed by hand into data/manual_fx_trans.csv from the BoI quarterly foreign-exchange-market report — no machine-readable series exists; every value carries its source passage in the CSV. History runs from 2018-Q4, all on the FX-market-report basis (figures from the Public's Assets portfolio release are a different measure and are never mixed in). Gaps: 2018-Q1–Q3, 2019-Q4, 2020-Q1, 2023-Q2 and 2024-Q3 have no institutions-only figure in a primary document (the Q3-2024 report's own docx says institutions moved to net purchases that quarter but prints no amount). SECONDARY ROW: 2020-Q2 (-2.0) comes from Funder relaying the Hebrew BoI release, not a BoI page — shown normally, flagged in the CSV. Figures are revised between reports — the Q1 2026 print of ~$5.2bn of sales was restated to ~$5.8bn in the Q2 report — which is why every seeded value carries its source.
why_on_board: The flow counterpart of the exposure rows: actual dollars bought or sold in the quarter, the cleanest read on whether institutions are moving money out or home.
what_a_rise_means: Institutions buying FX — taking money offshore.
what_a_fall_means: Net FX sales — repatriation, shekel-supportive.
read_with: Institutional FX exposure, USD / ILS

name: Institutional holdings: government bonds
definition: Tradable government bonds held by insurance companies, pension funds and provident/advanced-study funds, NIS bn, with the share of total market value alongside. New Report from January 2020; before that, Old Report percentage shares times market value (the splice is marked; government old/new levels agree to within 0.1%).
why_on_board: The core domestic bid for Israeli duration: when this share falls while supply rises, someone else must be found to hold the stock — usually at a higher yield.
what_a_rise_means: Institutions absorbing more of the government bond stock.
what_a_fall_means: The domestic bid stepping back — supply pressure on yields.
read_with: Net new supply (est., ex-price), Foreign ownership: government bonds

name: Institutional holdings: corporate bonds
definition: Tradable corporate bonds held by insurance, pension and provident funds, NIS bn, with the share of market value alongside. New Report from January 2020; Old Report before. CAUTION: the Old Report's corporate universe is 3-10% narrower than the New Report's over the 2020-2024 overlap, so the January 2020 splice is a basis break (institutional share reads ~1.5pp higher on the old basis at the splice).
why_on_board: The Tel Bond market's anchor holders; their appetite sets corporate spreads.
what_a_rise_means: Institutions adding credit — spread-supportive.
what_a_fall_means: Institutions cutting credit; spreads widen into less liquid hands.
read_with: Israel corporate spread, Tel Bond-60 CPI Linked

name: Institutional share of bonds outstanding
definition: Insurance + pension + provident holdings as a percent of ALL tradable government plus corporate bonds outstanding (the display shows the government and corporate legs; the numeric series is the combined share). Because prices move the numerator and denominator together, this gauge is undistorted by yield moves — the cleanest single line on whether institutions are gaining or ceding ground against supply. Old Report basis before the January 2020 splice.
why_on_board: Net supply and absorption in NIS bn both carry price effects; the share ratio cancels them, so a falling line means supply is genuinely outrunning the institutional bid.
what_a_rise_means: Institutions absorbing more than their share of new supply.
what_a_fall_means: Supply outrunning the institutional bid — someone else must take the stock.
read_with: Net new supply (est., ex-price), Institutional holdings: government bonds

name: Foreign residents' share: gov · corp
definition: Nonresidents' share of tradable government and corporate bonds on one line (the numeric series behind the sparkline is the government share). Same data as the Foreign ownership rows in Credit and risk premium, gathered here for the flows story.
why_on_board: Foreign and institutional demand are the two marginal buyers; this row keeps both sides of that ledger in one block.
what_a_rise_means: Foreign money adding Israeli bonds.
what_a_fall_means: Foreign money leaving — more for locals to absorb.
read_with: Foreign ownership: government bonds, Institutional holdings: government bonds

name: Mutual funds' share: corp · gov
definition: Mutual funds' holdings of tradable bonds as % of market value, from the same BoI distribution-of-holders files as the institutional and foreign rows — the numeric series is the CORPORATE share (Jul 2026: 47.9%, split 31.9% non-MMF investment funds + 16.0% money market funds), the display adds the government share (7.2%). From 2020-01 the series is the New Report's two fund sectors; before it, the Old Report's single Mutual funds column (clean splice: corp 33.8% Dec 2019 vs 33.2% Jan 2020). BASIS NOTES: the Oct-2018 ETN->ETF reform moved index-tracker holdings from 'Public and Other' into the mutual-fund column, so pre-2018 the column understates fund-intermediated holdings; pre-2020 corp is the narrower Old Report universe. RECONCILIATION: published references put mutual funds at ~34% (BoI FSR, mid-2024) and 37.3% (ISA, Jun 2024); this series prints 35.8% (Jun 2024) and 37.0% (Jul 2024) — differences are universe (the BoI file excludes convertibles, structured bonds and CDs), ETF treatment and valuation month. MMF+non-MMF columns ride the Bond holders tab.
why_on_board: The flow-driven holder: fund shares move with retail subscriptions and redemptions, the fastest-moving leg of the corporate bond demand base.
what_a_rise_means: Fund inflows absorbing more of the market — demand that can reverse quickly.
what_a_fall_means: Redemptions or rotation; a thinner flow-driven bid under corporate spreads.
read_with: Institutions + funds share of corp bonds, Institutional share of bonds outstanding, Israel corporate spread

name: Index-tracking funds classified to Israeli corp bonds (AUM, ISA)
definition: AUM of index-tracking vehicles — ETFs (קרנות סל) plus open tracking funds (קרנות מחקות) — whose ISA investment-policy classification is Israeli corporate bonds, expressed as % of the BoI tradable corporate bond MARKET VALUE of the same month. CLASSIFICATION IS NOT EXACT HOLDINGS: a fund classified to corporate bonds also holds some government bonds and cash, while general-bond trackers hold corporate paper that is NOT counted here — so this is a proxy for the tracking slice, not a holdings census. Seeded manually (data/manual_fund_holders.csv) from the ISA annual mutual-funds report with page-cited figures, each pairing verified against a rendered image of the page (the PDF's Hebrew text layer is visually reversed). First point, Dec 2024 (Table 1, p.10): trackers classified to corporate bonds held NIS 54.8bn (ETFs 27.98 + tracking funds 26.86) = 11.5% of the BoI corp market value, vs ALL mutual funds at 40.4% the same month; government-classified trackers held NIS 6.2bn (~0.9% of gov MV). The ISA corp class includes convertibles, which the BoI denominator excludes. The secondary line shows ALL mutual funds' corporate-bond share in the same month for comparison. No machine-readable source splits active vs tracking funds (probe rounds 31-34).
why_on_board: The rules-based core of the fund bid: tracking money must trade index rebalances mechanically — the index-rebalancing thesis variable.
what_a_rise_means: More mechanical, rebalance-driven flow in corporate bonds.
what_a_fall_means: Active managers regaining share of the fund bid.
read_with: Mutual funds' share: corp · gov, Assets tracking Tel Bond indices

name: Assets tracking Tel Bond indices
definition: Assets in products tracking the main Tel Bond indices (20 / 40 / 60 / Shekel / CPI-linked), NIS bn, with per-index columns on the export (IL_TRACK_TB20/TB40/TB60/TBSHK/TBCPI). MANUAL ROW, awaiting its first seed: the TASE tracking-products pages render client-side and the fund APIs reject CI requests (probe round 31), so figures are typed into data/manual_fund_holders.csv from TASE publications. Tracking assets as % of each index's market cap is an open follow-up — index market cap looks obtainable from the one working TASE endpoint.
why_on_board: Sizes the mechanical bid per index: how much money must trade each Tel Bond rebalance.
what_a_rise_means: A bigger passive bid under the tracked indices.
what_a_fall_means: Passive outflows; rebalance flows shrink.
read_with: — of which index-tracking (ETFs + index funds), Tel Bond 60

name: Institutions + funds share of corp bonds
definition: Institutions (insurance + pension + provident) PLUS mutual funds as a share of tradable corporate bond market value (Jul 2026: 81.6% = institutions 33.7% + funds 47.9%). Both legs come from the same BoI distribution-of-holders file, so the sum is on one consistent basis and the file's sectors sum to ~100 of market value (100.8% at Jul 2026, statistical discrepancy per the BoI's note). WHAT THE SUM MIXES: institutions are rule-bound mandates; money market funds are rule-bound by maturity and liquidity limits, and their investors can leave daily; the other investment funds are mostly ACTIVE managers (ETFs are inside this sector too, and the tracking split is the manual row above) — so the combined figure is NOT a passive or rules-based share, it is the slice of the market held by regulated intermediaries rather than direct accounts, nonresidents or banks. ISA published shares differ by universe and ETF treatment. Hedge funds cannot be separated — see the holder-sector footnote.
why_on_board: How much of the corporate market is held through regulated intermediaries — mandates and funds whose constraints and investor flows shape their trading — versus direct accounts, nonresidents and banks.
what_a_rise_means: More of the market held through intermediaries; mandate constraints and fund flows matter more for pricing.
what_a_fall_means: A thicker directly-held base (private accounts, nonresidents, banks).
read_with: Mutual funds' share: corp · gov, Institutional share of bonds outstanding, Israel corporate spread

name: Net new supply (est., ex-price)
definition: Net new tradable bond supply (government + corporate), NIS bn per complete quarter, NET OF THE ESTIMATED PRICE EFFECT: the change in market value outstanding less the start-of-quarter stock times a proxy index return (Tel Gov Shekel for the government stock, Tel Bond for the corporate stock) — an estimate, from 2009 where the corporate proxy begins. This is the board's headline figure, matching the chart's default view; the raw CHANGE IN MARKET VALUE rides the same row's display (e.g. Q2 2026: +30.8 est. · +78.4 MV, where the +78bn decomposed to roughly +48bn price effect at ~-43bp of yield and ~+31bn ex-price flow) and keeps its own export columns. Makam is excluded — central-bank bills are liquidity management, not bond supply. The BoI files publish no par values, which is why the price adjustment is an estimate. No change is computed across the January 2020 Old/New Report splice (the straddling quarter is dropped).
source: BoI distribution-of-holders files (market value column) less the TASE proxy-index price effect — automated
why_on_board: The denominator of the demand story: how much new paper the market had to absorb each quarter, shown next to gross issuance so refinancing is visible.
what_a_rise_means: More genuinely new paper to absorb (issuance net of redemptions rising).
what_a_fall_means: The stock shrinking ex-price (redemptions exceed issuance).
read_with: Gross business-sector bond issuance, Gross government borrowing, Institutional holdings: government bonds

name: Institutional absorption (est., ex-price)
definition: Change in insurance + pension + provident holdings of tradable government plus corporate bonds, NIS bn per complete quarter, NET OF THE ESTIMATED PRICE EFFECT (same proxy indices as ex-price net supply: Tel Gov Shekel on the government stock, Tel Bond on the corporate stock) — an estimate, from 2009 where the corporate proxy begins. The display pairs it with the raw CHANGE IN MARKET VALUE (e.g. Q2 2026: +3.5 est. · +22.2 MV) and the secondary line shows the share of ex-price net supply absorbed (Q2 2026: ~11%) — both only when the figures land on the same complete quarter, and the share only while ex-price supply is meaningfully positive. The BoI files publish no par values, which is why the price adjustment is an estimate; no change is computed across the January 2020 Old/New Report splice.
source: BoI distribution-of-holders files (holder columns) less the TASE proxy-index price effect — automated
why_on_board: The demand half of the supply row above it: how much of the quarter's genuinely new paper the local institutions took, the cleanest flow read on their bond appetite.
what_a_rise_means: Institutions absorbing more of the new supply — domestic demand carrying the market.
what_a_fall_means: Institutions stepping back ex-price; other holders must absorb the issuance.
read_with: Net new supply (est., ex-price), Institutional share of bonds outstanding, Institutional holdings: government bonds

name: Gross business-sector bond issuance
definition: Gross tradable bond issuance by the nonfinancial business sector, NIS bn per quarter, typed into data/manual_issuance.csv from the BoI quarterly 'Debt Developments in the Nonfinancial Private Sector' release (no Series Database equivalent exists; OZAR_90_M was checked and is government ministries expenditure, not issuance). History runs from 2018-Q1. DEFINITION CHANGE 2019: from 2019-Q1 the BoI excludes credit card companies as well as banks and insurers; 2018 figures exclude banks and insurers only — a small basis break at 2019-Q1. Gaps: 2020-Q3, 2020-Q4, 2022-Q2 and 2022-Q4 (releases give no issuance figure in readable form). SECONDARY ROWS: 2021-Q3, 2021-Q4, 2022-Q1 and 2022-Q3 come from financial press (Funder, hon.co.il, ICE) quoting the BoI release — shown normally, flagged in the CSV.
why_on_board: Gross issuance against net supply shows how much of the market's absorption burden is refinancing versus genuinely new money.
what_a_rise_means: Corporates leaning harder on the bond market.
what_a_fall_means: Issuance windows closing, or loans replacing bonds.
read_with: Net new supply (est., ex-price), Israel corporate spread

name: Gross government borrowing
definition: Gross government borrowing, NIS bn per year, from the Accountant General / MoF annual debt reports (data/manual_issuance.csv; annual stamps). History 2009-2025, no gaps: 2012 (125) and 2014 (107) are quoted directly from the MoF Annual Debt Reports. The domestic tradable amount and its share of gross borrowing ride the export columns (IL_GOV_BORROW_TRADABLE, IL_GOV_BORROW_TRD_SHARE; share computed from the two amounts, 2025: ~85%); in early years tradable includes switch auctions and green-shoe allotments. The 2012 (97) and 2013 (82) tradable amounts are sums of components quoted in the same report (domestic funding minus non-tradable; the 2013 figure cross-checks net funding 21 + redemptions 61) — marked COMPUTED FROM QUOTED COMPONENTS in the CSV. SECONDARY ROW: 2023 (160 / 116 tradable) comes from ICE reporting on the annual debt report — shown normally, flagged in the CSV.
source: Accountant General annual debt report — manual (data/manual_issuance.csv)
why_on_board: The sovereign's call on the market each year — the slow-moving anchor of the supply side that the quarterly rows fluctuate around.
what_a_rise_means: A bigger borrowing programme: more duration for the market to carry.
what_a_fall_means: Fiscal consolidation; less supply pressure.
read_with: Net new supply (est., ex-price), Israel 10Y

name: Bond-holder sector definitions (footnote)
definition: The export's holder-breakdown blocks use the BoI's own categories. New Report (from 2020-01), definitions quoted from the files: Nonfinancial Corporations = 'Companies classified as nonfinancial corporations by the Central Bureau of Statistics + nonfinancial companies for which there isn't a sectoral classification by the Central Bureau of Statistics'; Other Financial Corporations = 'Financial corporations excluding banks, mutual funds, and institutional investors'; NPISHs = 'Nonprofit Institutions Serving Households'. Old Report (before 2020): 'Public and Other' was 'a remainder - the difference between the total and the other holdings ... includes, among other things, households' and the business sector's holdings, short sales, and more'. HEDGE FUNDS / PRIVATE INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS: no BoI document we could find states their classification explicitly. In the Old Report they sat inside the 'Public and Other' residual (quoted above). In the New Report, by the quoted definitions they are not mutual funds, not institutional investors, not banks — so (INFERENCE, not a quoted classification) an Israeli fund organized as a financial corporation lands in Other Financial Corporations, an unclassified company in Nonfinancial Corporations, and holdings via investors' personal accounts in Households.
source: BoI distribution-of-holders files, Explanations sheets and footnotes
why_on_board: Footnote for the holder-breakdown export: what each sector means, and where hedge funds sit.
read_with: Institutional share of bonds outstanding

name: PIMIX (reconstructed TR)
definition: The PIMCO Income Fund (institutional class) as a reconstructed total-return series — an actively managed multi-sector bond fund, distributions reinvested.
why_on_board: The strongest widely held active bond competitor: it is the 'why not just buy PIMIX' answer the fund must have, tracked on identical total-return terms.
what_a_rise_means: The active-bond alternative performing strongly.
what_a_fall_means: The comparison fund struggling — active dollar credit underperforming.
read_with: AGG (TR), the tracker's Combined feed

name: BND (reconstructed TR)
definition: The Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF as a reconstructed total-return series, distributions reinvested on the ex-date.
why_on_board: A second, independently constructed read on the same US core bond market — when AGG and BND diverge, it flags a data problem rather than a market move.
what_a_rise_means: US investment-grade bond market gaining.
what_a_fall_means: US bond market losing ground.
read_with: AGG (TR), PIMIX (TR)

name: AGG (reconstructed TR)
definition: The iShares Core US Aggregate Bond ETF with distributions reinvested on the ex-date — a true total-return series reconstructed from raw closes and corrected distributions.
source: Yahoo raw close + corrected distributions (see workbook Notes)
why_on_board: The fund's stated benchmark universe includes the US aggregate: this row is the dollar bond market the strategy must beat, measured the same way the tracker measures it.
what_a_rise_means: US core bonds rallying — the passive alternative is performing.
what_a_fall_means: The benchmark losing ground — Israeli carry has an easier bar.
read_with: BND (TR), Benchmarks tabs in the Excel, Tel Bond 60

name: Global Aggregate (AGGG.L)
definition: A UCITS ETF tracking the Bloomberg Global Aggregate — global investment-grade bonds across currencies — used as a price proxy (income not reinvested here).
why_on_board: It places both the US and Israeli books in the global bond tide: when the global aggregate moves, judging local skill means netting that tide out first.
what_a_rise_means: Global bond markets rallying together.
what_a_fall_means: A global bond sell-off — local weakness may not be local at all.
read_with: AGG (TR), US 10Y, Israel 10Y

name: Tel Bond-60 CPI Linked
definition: TASE's index of the sixty largest CPI-linked, fixed-coupon corporate bonds — the flagship benchmark of Israel's linker credit market, calculated as a gross total return index (TASE: "Index Calculation Method: GTR"). Constituents are rated at least A− by Maalot or A3 by Midroog (foreign series AA/Aa2), capped at 4% per bond and 20% per issuer, with a monthly review on market cap.
source: TASE Data Hub daily; TASE end-of-day history file
why_on_board: The closest public benchmark to what the fund's managers actually hold; it is also a named benchmark in the monthly report. Its level and spread behaviour are the strategy's home market.
what_a_rise_means: Israeli CPI-linked credit gaining — carry plus inflation compensation working.
what_a_fall_means: Local linker credit under pressure: spreads widening or real yields rising.
read_with: Tel Bond Shekel, Israel 10Y breakeven, Israel corporate spread (Phase 3)

name: Tel Bond Shekel 100
definition: TASE's index of the hundred largest fixed-rate (unlinked) shekel corporate bonds, price basis.
source: TASE Data Hub daily; Investing.com seed
why_on_board: The nominal half of Israeli corporate credit. Together with Tel Bond-60 it splits manager performance into rates, inflation and credit components.
what_a_rise_means: Nominal shekel credit gaining — falling yields or tightening spreads.
what_a_fall_means: Nominal corporates under pressure.
read_with: Tel Bond-60, Tel Gov Shekel, BoI rate

name: Tel Gov Shekel
definition: TASE's index of fixed-rate shekel government bonds, price basis — the tradable expression of the Israeli nominal government curve.
source: TASE Data Hub daily; Investing.com seed
why_on_board: The government leg that turns the corporate indices into spread reads: Tel Bond moves matching Tel Gov are rates; the residual is credit.
what_a_rise_means: Shekel govies rallying (yields falling).
what_a_fall_means: Government duration selling off.
read_with: Israel 10Y, Tel Bond Shekel, Tel Bond-60

name: S&P 500 total return
definition: Standard & Poor's own total-return index for the S&P 500 — price plus reinvested dividends, the institutional standard for US equity performance.
why_on_board: The tracker benchmarks against equity as well as bonds: this is the equity bar, on the same total-return basis as the reconstructed bond series.
what_a_rise_means: US equities compounding — the risk-asset alternative is winning.
what_a_fall_means: Equity weakness — bond carry looks relatively better.
read_with: S&P 500 (price), VIX, the tracker's Combined feed

name: Nasdaq Composite
definition: All Nasdaq-listed stocks, price basis — the broadest read on US technology and growth.
why_on_board: Growth equities are the long-duration end of risk assets: they move with real yields, so they double as a cross-check on the rates rows.
what_a_rise_means: Risk appetite for long-duration growth assets rising.
what_a_fall_means: Growth de-rating — often alongside rising real yields.
read_with: Nasdaq 100, US 10Y real yield

name: Nasdaq 100
definition: The hundred largest non-financial Nasdaq companies, price basis — big tech in one number.
why_on_board: The concentration of the US market in mega-cap tech means this index often IS the market's direction; the letter references it monthly.
what_a_rise_means: Mega-cap tech leading markets higher.
what_a_fall_means: The market's leadership faltering.
read_with: Nasdaq Composite, S&P 500

name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
definition: Thirty large US blue-chip companies, price-weighted — the oldest running gauge of the US equity market.
why_on_board: The value/industrial counterpoint to the Nasdaq: when the Dow leads, the rally is broad, not just tech.
what_a_rise_means: Old-economy blue chips gaining — broad, value-led strength.
what_a_fall_means: Cyclical/industrial weakness.
read_with: S&P 500, Russell 2000

name: Russell 2000
definition: Two thousand US small-cap companies, price basis — the market segment most sensitive to domestic financial conditions.
why_on_board: Small caps feel rate and credit conditions first: they corroborate (or contradict) what the credit spread rows are saying.
what_a_rise_means: Financial conditions easing for smaller borrowers.
what_a_fall_means: Tightening biting the economy's periphery first.
read_with: US HY OAS, US IG OAS

name: TA-125
definition: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's 125 largest companies — Israel's headline equity index (level as published by TASE).
why_on_board: Israeli equity is the fastest read on how markets price Israel's economy and security situation — context for every Israeli bond position, and a named line in the monthly letter.
what_a_rise_means: Confidence in Israeli assets improving.
what_a_fall_means: Israel risk-off — usually echoed in the shekel and CDS.
read_with: TA-35, 5Y CDS, USD/ILS

name: TA-35
definition: The 35 largest TASE companies — Israel's blue-chip index.
why_on_board: The large-cap core of the Israeli market; its gap to the TA-90 shows whether moves are broad or concentrated.
what_a_rise_means: Israeli large caps gaining.
what_a_fall_means: Blue-chip weakness.

name: TA-90
definition: The 90 next-largest TASE companies after the TA-35 — Israel's mid-cap segment.
why_on_board: Mid caps are the domestically exposed part of the market — more sensitive to the local cycle the fund's credit books live in.
what_a_rise_means: The domestic Israeli economy being priced up.
what_a_fall_means: Local-cycle weakness beyond the blue chips.
read_with: TA-35, TA-125, Israel CPI

name: US Dollar Index (DXY)
definition: The ICE dollar index — the dollar against a basket of six major currencies (euro-heavy).
why_on_board: Separates 'the shekel moved' from 'the dollar moved': USD/ILS read against DXY shows which side of the cross is doing the work.
what_a_rise_means: Broad dollar strength — EM and Israeli assets typically face headwinds.
what_a_fall_means: Dollar weakness — supportive for non-US assets including the shekel.
read_with: USD/ILS, implied hedge cost

name: WTI crude
definition: The price of West Texas Intermediate crude oil in dollars per barrel (front-month futures).
why_on_board: Oil is both a global inflation input and Israel's key imported cost; it feeds the region's risk premium in ways CDS shows only later.
what_a_rise_means: Inflation pressure and, often, Middle-East risk premium rising.
what_a_fall_means: Disinflationary relief; lower import costs for Israel.
read_with: US CPI, Israel CPI, 5Y CDS

name: USD / EUR
definition: The dollar–euro exchange rate (dollars per euro as published by FRED).
why_on_board: The world's most traded currency pair — context for the basket moves that drive the shekel's effective rate.
what_a_rise_means: Euro firmer against the dollar.
what_a_fall_means: Dollar strength against the euro.
read_with: DXY, ILS basket

name: USD / ILS
definition: How many shekels one dollar buys — the exchange rate that converts every Israeli position into the fund's dollar accounting.
why_on_board: The single largest un-hedged risk a dollar fund holding shekel assets can carry. Even fully hedged, its level drives hedge rebalancing and local sentiment.
what_a_rise_means: Shekel weakening: unhedged shekel positions lose in dollars; often tracks risk-off on Israel.
what_a_fall_means: Shekel strengthening: dollar value of shekel assets rising.
read_with: Implied hedge cost, DXY, 5Y CDS

name: EUR / ILS
definition: Shekels per euro — Israel's second reference cross, covering its largest trading partner bloc.
why_on_board: Israel's trade is euro-heavy: EUR/ILS often explains basket moves that USD/ILS alone cannot.
what_a_rise_means: Shekel weaker against the euro.
what_a_fall_means: Shekel stronger against the euro.
read_with: USD/ILS, ILS basket

name: GBP / ILS
definition: Shekels per pound sterling.
why_on_board: A third independent cross that helps triangulate whether a move is shekel-specific or dollar-specific.
what_a_rise_means: Shekel weaker against sterling.
what_a_fall_means: Shekel stronger against sterling.
read_with: EUR/ILS, USD/ILS

name: ILS nominal effective (basket)
definition: The Bank of Israel's trade-weighted index of the shekel against its partners' currencies — the shekel's overall level, not one cross.
source: Bank of Israel API (nominal effective exchange rate)
why_on_board: The BoI watches the basket, not USD/ILS, when weighing intervention and the inflation pass-through — so this is the currency number that feeds policy.
what_a_rise_means: Broad shekel strength: disinflationary, weighs on exporters, raises intervention odds.
what_a_fall_means: Broad shekel weakness: imported inflation pressure; BoI attention.
read_with: USD/ILS, EUR/ILS, Israel CPI

name: Israel FX reserves ($B)
definition: The Bank of Israel's total foreign exchange reserves in billions of dollars — the month-end figure from the Bank's monthly reserves release, published in the first days of the following month.
why_on_board: Reserves are the BoI's ammunition to defend the shekel in a crisis — the depth of the backstop under every hedged position the fund holds.
what_a_rise_means: The war chest growing (accumulation or valuation gains).
what_a_fall_means: Reserves being spent — possibly defending the shekel; watch alongside USD/ILS.
read_with: USD/ILS, ILS basket
